title: Explicit adjunction for localization on a finite-limit site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-topos] with finite limits and let $U\in\mathcal C$. Give $\mathcal C/U$ the localized topology: a family covers if its underlying family covers in $\mathcal C$. For a sheaf $A$ on $\mathcal C$ define $j_U^{-1}A$ on $\mathcal C/U$ by $(j_U^{-1}A)(W\to U)=A(W)$, with the same restrictions. For a sheaf $G$ on $\mathcal C/U$ define $(j_{U,*}G)(V)=G(V\times U\to U)$, with restriction induced by $V'\times U\to V\times U$. These are sheaves, these formulas define functors, and there is an adjunction $j_U^{-1}\dashv j_{U,*}$ with left exact left adjoint, hence a geometric morphism $j_U$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. At $W\xrightarrow{t}U$, the counit $(j_U^{-1}j_{U,*}G)(W\to U)\to G(W\to U)$ is the restriction $G(W\times U\to U)\to G(W\to U)$ along the graph $(1_W,t):W\to W\times U$.

source.place: Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products), especially clause (3); Tag 00Y2 (lemma-restrict-back), restriction/counit computation. The slice-topos equivalence itself is already in lem-trf-topos-localization-site-presentation and lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction.

proof.text: Use covering families and the equalizer sheaf condition of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1). This is legitimate also for the sieve convention of [def-weil-pbc-topos], without replacing $\mathcal C$: take all small families whose generated sieve is covering. Isomorphism covers follow from the maximal-sieve axiom; base change follows from pullback stability, since finite limits exist; composite families cover by transitivity (pulling their generated sieve back to each member of the first family contains the covering sieve of the second family). The family and sieve sheaf conditions agree directly: compatible sections $x_i$ on a family define $x_f=F(a)(x_i)$ whenever $f=f_i a$ in its generated sieve. Two such factorizations give the same section by restriction to $V_i\times_V V_j$; conversely a sieve matching family restricts to compatible sections on its generating family. Every covering sieve is generated by its own arrows, a small family. Thus the unique amalgamations are the same. We use these covering families below.

source.place: Tag 00ZC (lemma-site-gives-topology), comparison of the two sheaf conditions; the converse construction here is the elementary finite-limit specialization of the sieve axioms

proof.text: The category $\mathcal C/U$ is small: its objects and arrows are subsets of the object/arrow data of $\mathcal C$ with a specified arrow to $U$. The site axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) pass to it: isomorphisms and composites are computed in $\mathcal C$, and the pullback of arrows over $U$ is their pullback in $\mathcal C$, equipped with the common composite to $U$. For a cover $\{W_i\to W\}$ over $U$, the sheaf equalizer for $RA(W\to U)=A(W)$ is exactly that for $A$ on this underlying cover, including the same pairwise fibre products. Hence $RA$ is a sheaf. Restricting a natural transformation to these same components defines $R$ on morphisms and preserves identities and composites.

source.place: Tag 00Y0 (definition-localize) and the following restriction formula

proof.text: Write $v(V)=(V\times U\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2}U)$ and $v(q)=q\times1_U$. The product universal property gives $v(1)=1$ and $v(qr)=v(q)v(r)$. For a cover $\{V_i\to V\}$, its base change along $V\times U\to V$ is the covering $\{V_i\times U\to V\times U\}$, and $(V_i\times U)\times_{V\times U}(V_j\times U)\cong(V_i\times_V V_j)\times U$ over $U$, by the pullback universal property. The equalizer for the sheaf $G$ on this cover over $U$ is therefore precisely the sheaf equalizer for $HG(V)=G(v(V))$ on the original cover. Thus $HG$ is a sheaf. Precomposition with $v$ on sections and on natural transformations defines the functor $H$, with exactly the asserted restrictions.

source.place: Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products), base-change proof of continuity and clause (3)

proof.text: For sheaves $A,G$ and a natural transformation $a:RA\to G$, define $b:A\to HG$ by $b_V=a_{v(V)}\circ A(\mathrm{pr}_1:V\times U\to V)$. For $q:V'\to V$, naturality of $a$ along $q\times1_U$ and $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ(q\times1_U)=q\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$ give $G(q\times1_U)b_V=b_{V'}A(q)$. This proves that $b$ is a sheaf morphism, since the categories of sheaves are full subcategories of the presheaf categories [def-weil-pbc-topos].

source.place: Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products); explicit Hom-map induced by the product projections

proof.text: Conversely, for $b:A\to HG$ and $t:W\to U$, put $\gamma_t=(1_W,t): (W\xrightarrow t U)\to v(W)$ and $a_t=G(\gamma_t)\circ b_W$. If $q:(W',t')\to(W,t)$ is over $U$, then $\gamma_t q=(q\times1_U)\gamma_{t'}$. This identity and naturality of $b$ give $G(q)a_t=a_{t'}A(q)$. Thus $a:RA\to G$ is a sheaf morphism. Both constructions commute with precomposition by any morphism of $A$ and postcomposition by any morphism of $G$, by naturality of those morphisms along the displayed projections and graphs.

source.place: Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products); explicit inverse Hom-map induced by the graph

proof.text: Starting with $a$, the round trip at $t:W\to U$ is $G(\gamma_t)a_{v(W)}A(\mathrm{pr}_1)=a_t A(\gamma_t)A(\mathrm{pr}_1)=a_t$, because $\mathrm{pr}_1\gamma_t=1_W$. Starting with $b$, the round trip at $V$ is $G(\gamma_{\mathrm{pr}_2})b_{V\times U}A(\mathrm{pr}_1)$. Naturality of $b$ along $\mathrm{pr}_1:V\times U\to V$ identifies this with $G(\gamma_{\mathrm{pr}_2})G(\mathrm{pr}_1\times1_U)b_V=b_V$, since $(\mathrm{pr}_1\times1_U)\gamma_{\mathrm{pr}_2}=1_{V\times U}$. The two natural Hom-maps are therefore mutually inverse, giving $R\dashv H$. The counit is the image of $1_{HG}$ under the second Hom-map: at $t:W\to U$ it is $G(\gamma_t):G(W\times U\to U)\to G(W\to U)$, exactly the claimed restriction.

source.place: Tag 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products); elementary verification of the adjunction and its counit

proof.text: For any finite diagram $(A_i)$ in $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise](1) computes its limit at $W$ as $\lim_i A_i(W)$, and computes the limit of $(RA_i)$ on $\mathcal C/U$ at $W\to U$ by the very same set and projection maps. The canonical comparison is the identity at every object, so $R$ preserves finite limits, including the empty diagram. The two sheaf categories are Grothendieck topoi by their small-site presentations [def-weil-pbc-topos]. The functors $R,H$, the adjunction just constructed, and preservation of finite limits consequently give the geometric morphism $j_U$ by [def-trf-geometric-morphism].

lean.statement: theorem slice_subtopos_site_presentation {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [HasFiniteLimits C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (U : C) : ∃ j : GeometricMorphism (Sheaf (J.over U) (Type (max u w))) (Sheaf J (Type (max u w))), j.inverse = J.overPullback (Type (max u w)) U ∧ (∀ (G : Sheaf (J.over U) (Type (max u w))) (V : C), (j.direct.obj G).obj.obj (op V) = G.obj.obj (op (Over.mk (Limits.prod.snd : Limits.prod V U ⟶ U)))) ∧ (∀ (G : Sheaf (J.over U) (Type (max u w))) (V V' : C) (q : V' ⟶ V), HEq ((j.direct.obj G).obj.map q.op) (G.obj.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (Limits.prod.snd : Limits.prod V' U ⟶ U)) (V := Over.mk (Limits.prod.snd : Limits.prod V U ⟶ U)) (Limits.prod.map q (𝟙 U))).op)) ∧ (∀ (G G' : Sheaf (J.over U) (Type (max u w))) (f : G ⟶ G') (V : C), HEq ((j.direct.map f).hom.app (op V)) (f.hom.app (op (Over.mk (Limits.prod.snd : Limits.prod V U ⟶ U))))) ∧ ∀ (G : Sheaf (J.over U) (Type (max u w))) (W : C) (t : W ⟶ U), HEq ((j.adj.counit.app G).hom.app (op (Over.mk t))) (G.obj.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk t) (V := Over.mk (Limits.prod.snd : Limits.prod W U ⟶ U)) (Limits.prod.lift (𝟙 W) t)).op)
